subject: Intermittent DB timeouts over private link — possible SNAT/route mismatch
messages:
From: Sam Brown <sam.brown@clearwave.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Cc: ClearWave Eng <eng@clearwave.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Dec 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: [ClearWave] Sporadic DB timeouts via private link — immediate help needed

Hannah,

We started seeing sporadic 502/timeout errors from our on-prem app when it talks to the DB hosted behind the private attachment (Redwood private deployment). Impact started ~13:30 PST and is ongoing in short bursts. Our ops team captured a short pcap and a traceroute from the app host (attached).

Symptoms:
- 1–3 minute windows where DB queries time out (new connections fail)
- Traceroute shows the last hop from our app to the private edge is OK but replies sometimes appear to return over the internet path
- Firewall logs show a sudden spike in conntrack entries from our app host to DB port around the same timestamps

We suspect either a NAT change on our appliance or an asymmetric route somewhere that is exhausting conntrack and causing failures. Can you escalate to networking? This is affecting production.

Attachments: clearwave_pcap.pcap, edge_traceroute.txt

Thanks,
Sam Brown
Sr. SRE, ClearWave Analytics

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 9 Dec 2026 09:10:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: [ClearWave] Sporadic DB timeouts via private link — immediate help needed

Sam / Hannah — quick triage notes after looking at the pcap + edge path: 

1) Asymmetric return observed
   - The pcap shows SYN from app -> DB goes to our private attachment IP as expected. SYN-ACKs intermittently return with an outer source IP that belongs to ClearWave's internet egress address space (not the private peering). That indicates a SNAT on their side or a policy that sends responses out the internet path.

2) Conntrack spike consistent with SNAT changes
   - Our conntrack_dump shows a spike of ephemeral entries from the ephemeral source ports used by the app. When replies come back via different egress, the NATed 5-tuple doesn't match and connections time out while conntrack table fills. See attached conntrack_dump.txt.

3) Route propagation / host route mismatch
   - I queried BGP advertisements from the private attachment and we are seeing clearwave/32 host routes flapping occasionally. If the customer deployed an on-prem SNAT appliance that momentarily removes the host route and re-advertises via the internet router, that will cause asymmetry.

Immediate ask for ClearWave:
- Rollback any recent SNAT rules on your perimeter firewall (if that change occurred around 13:30 PST yesterday).
- If SNAT is required for some flows, ensure SNAT is applied only for internet-bound ranges and NOT for the private prefix that reaches Redwood's private attachment.

From our side we will: 
- Put the private edge into debug mode to capture BGP update timings and next-hop changes for your routes.
- Watch conntrack pressure and fail open if necessary to avoid outages while you rollback.

Attaching: conntrack_dump.txt (excerpt).

— Marcus Lin
Network Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Sam Brown <sam.brown@clearwave.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>

Marcus — thank you, this aligns with what we found. We did push a firewall rule yesterday morning that added a generic SNAT for 'outbound' flows as an emergency mitigation for an unrelated issue. I didn't realize it would affect private peering.

We are going to rollback that SNAT and keep you posted. Attached are firewall logs showing the SNAT translation timestamps (fw_logs_snats.csv). We will coordinate a rollback at 12:00 PST and will run a continuous traceroute during the window.

Sam
From: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>

Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Dec 2026 11:20:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: [ClearWave] Sporadic DB timeouts via private link — immediate help needed

Sam — quick post-mortem and recommended mitigation plan after your rollback: 

Summary:
- Root cause: Customer-side SNAT applied to flows destined for Redwood private prefix, causing asymmetric return paths and conntrack exhaustion on the firewall.
- Impact window: 2026-12-08 13:30–15:10 PST (matches conntrack spike and route flaps).

Immediate remediation completed:
- ClearWave rolled back the emergency SNAT at 12:00 PST today; we observed stable BGP advertisement of the /32 host routes and SYN/SYN-ACK symmetry confirmed in captures.

Follow-up actions (recommended):
1) Add an ACL rule to explicitly avoid SNAT for Redwood-advertised prefixes (apply order: exception before generic SNAT).
2) On ClearWave firewall: reduce conntrack timeout for failed handshakes to reclaim table entries faster during transient events.
3) On Redwood edge: apply MTU clamp 1400 on the attachment EGRESS path temporarily to avoid fragmentation issues we observed intermittently in the pcap.
4) Both parties: schedule a coordinated maintenance window for a controlled SNAT test (JIRA NETOPS-7213).

I'll draft a short runbook and share it in the Drive link (shared above) with example iptables/snats and the traceroute checklist. If you want, we can schedule a 1hr call Monday to walk through the runbook and perform a safe test.

Thanks for quick coordination — happy to close after the test window completes.

— Dev Patel
Senior Engineer, Private Deployments — Redwood Inference
